title: Temporary spike leases: metering, throttle fallback, and invoice attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Some Dedicated customers need the ability to absorb short, unexpected request spikes without immediately paying high overage rates or experiencing hard throttles. We propose a temporary spike-lease mechanism: customers can automatically borrow a small pool of amortized capacity (time-limited leases) that is metered separately and attributed on invoices as an adjustable line item. Goals: 1) preserve latency SLOs for short spikes, 2) provide transparent billing attribution and amortization to reduce invoice surprise, 3) offer operator controls to tune eviction/throttle behavior for fairness and fraud prevention.
acceptance_criteria: Spike-lease can be enabled per-tenant with configurable max qps and expiry window (default 10s window, configurable to 120s)
System meters lease usage separately from committed capacity and records per-tenant lease consumption in billing tables with amortization flags
When lease quota is exhausted, system gracefully falls back to tenant-specific throttle policy (not global hard throttle) and emits clear events for Console and alerts
Invoices include a distinct line item showing lease usage, amortized cost, and effective unit price with link to usage breakdown
Operator UI: ability to revoke leases for a tenant, inspect active leases, and view recent lease allocation history
End-to-end test harness simulates spikes and validates SLO and billing attribution within +/- 2% on aggregated cost estimates

design_decisions: Amortization window: default 1 hour for invoice smoothing; lease consumption is recorded at request time but cost is spread across the invoice period to avoid spikes in single invoice
Per-tenant cap: leases limited to a percentage of the tenant's committed throughput (default 10%) to bound cost exposure
Expiry semantics: two levels — soft expiry (no new lease tokens issued) and hard expiry (active tokens invalidated) to allow graceful draining
Fallback behavior: prefer tenant-configured throttles (token-bucket penalties) rather than global hard limits to avoid noisy neighbors
Metering granularity: 1-second resolution for runtime enforcement, 1-minute aggregates for billing to minimize table cardinality
Fraud mitigation: require usage history threshold to auto-enable leases; new tenants need manual opt-in for first 14 days
tradeoffs: Complexity vs clarity: Separating lease metering from overage simplifies operator reasoning but increases pipeline joins in billing reports
Predictability vs availability: Larger leases improve latency during spikes but increase billing exposure; default conservative caps chosen
Accuracy vs cost: Fine-grained metering yields better invoice accuracy but higher storage/cost — we choose 1m aggregate for billing to balance both
Latency vs enforcement: Enforcing leases synchronously in scheduler adds small path overhead (~0.2ms) but prevents oversubscription; measured impact acceptable in perf tests
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): internal + 3 alpha customers, feature-flag ON, close monitoring for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (beta): invite-only for larger set of customers with billing opt-in, surface lease line item in invoices
Phase 3 (general): enabled by default with opt-out button and operator adjustable caps
Rollback: immediately disable lease token issuance via operator flag; existing tokens expire within configured hard expiry window
Post-release: 30/60/90-day usage review to tune default caps and amortization window
metrics: p50/p95 latency for dedicated tenants during spike windows (should not regress >5%)
Lease-allocation rate (leases/sec) and average lease duration
Lease consumption as % of committed throughput
Number of fallback throttle events per tenant
Invoice variance: weekly predicted vs actual cost delta attributable to leases
Chargeback accuracy: % of lease cost correctly attributed to tenant in billing exports
